sources.entry: Databag - Federated, end-to-end encrypted messaging service for the web, iOS, and Android, supporting text, photos, video, and WebRTC video and audio calls. Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Databag is a self-hostable, federated messenger with end-to-end encryption and topic-based threads, with clients for web, iOS, and Android.
summary.what_it_does: Databag is a messaging server you run yourself, paired with apps for browsers, iOS, and Android (the README says the app is on F-Droid, Google Play, and the Apple App Store). Accounts on different nodes can talk to each other via federation. Conversations are organized as topic-based threads rather than contacts, with no stated limit on group members. The README says topics can be sealed with end-to-end encryption so the hosting admin cannot read them. Text, photos, video, and audio/video calls are supported, with calls relying on a separate STUN/TURN relay for NAT traversal. Mobile alerts are sent via UnifiedPush, FCM, or APN, and multi-factor authentication works with TOTP apps. The README says the server is lightweight enough to run on a Raspberry Pi Zero v1.3.
use_cases: private messaging on a home server
running a chat node on a Raspberry Pi
self-hosted audio and video calls with a TURN relay
how_to_run: From the net/container sub directory: docker-compose -f compose.yaml -p databag up

For HTTPS with certbot: create a DNS entry, edit net/container/docker-compose-swag.yml with your domain, then from the project root run: docker-compose -f net/container/docker-compose-swag.yml -p databag up
Alternatively, run the balzack/databag:latest image (port 7000, ADMIN environment variable for the admin password, volume at /var/lib/databag)
Put the node behind a reverse proxy with a valid certificate (README gives Nginx Proxy Manager and nginx-proxy examples)
In the browser, open the server address, log in to admin settings, set the Federated Host, then generate an account link
notable: Federated design where accounts on separate nodes can communicate, with identity based on public-private keys rather than a domain or blockchain
Sealed topics that are end-to-end encrypted so the node admin cannot view them
Runs on arm64 and amd64 containers and is described as light enough for a Raspberry Pi Zero
One-click install listings for CapRover, CasaOS, Unraid, Runtipi, Kubero, and Umbrel
caveats: Audio and video calls need a separate STUN/TURN relay server; the README offers coturn or Cloudflare TURN, and a demo relay for testing only
You need a DNS name pointing to your node with a certificate; the README says a container service is much easier than a manual deploy
The public test server is regularly wiped, so it should not be used for important content
keywords: chat with my family on my own server
